paragraphs.title: Babylon’s Connection with Judah and the Babylonian Envoys’ Visit

answers: The king of Babylon
Isaiah the prophet
Hezekiah’s fathers
easy.explanation: Merodach-baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a present to Hezekiah.
easy.q: Who sent letters and a present to Hezekiah?

answers: To take Hezekiah’s treasures
Because he had heard that Hezekiah had been sick and was recovered
To ask Isaiah a question
easy.explanation: The king had heard that Hezekiah had been sick and had recovered.
easy.q: Why did the king of Babylon send the messengers?

answers: Only his house
Only the silver vessels
All his treasures and possessions
easy.explanation: Hezekiah showed them the silver, gold, spices, precious ointment, armour, and everything in his treasures.
easy.q: What did Hezekiah show the Babylonian visitors?

answers: He was glad of them
He hid them
He rebuked them
medium.explanation: The KJV says, “And Hezekiah was glad of them.”
medium.q: How did Hezekiah respond to the visit of the Babylonian envoys?

answers: He showed them nothing
He revealed the full extent of his wealth to them
He gave them the kingdom
medium.explanation: The passage says there was nothing in his house or dominion that he did not show them.
medium.q: What does Hezekiah’s showing the envoys everything in his treasures indicate?

answers: A gift
An illness
A palace
medium.explanation: The king of Babylon sent Hezekiah a gift, or present.
medium.q: What does the word “present” mean in verse 1?

answers: The gesture led Hezekiah to show his treasures
The gesture caused Hezekiah to hide his treasures
The gesture was meant to return Judah’s treasures
challenge.explanation: After receiving the letters and present, Hezekiah was glad and showed the envoys all his possessions.
challenge.q: What connection does the passage make between Babylon’s gesture and Hezekiah’s treasures?

answers: He showed them only the gold
There was nothing that he did not show them
He showed them only the house of his precious things
challenge.explanation: The passage emphasizes that Hezekiah showed them everything in his house and dominion.
challenge.q: Which detail especially emphasizes the extent of Hezekiah’s disclosure?

answers: The visit was connected with Hezekiah’s condition
The envoys came as enemies during a war
The envoys came because Hezekiah requested treasures
challenge.explanation: The verse directly connects Hezekiah’s recovery with the Babylonian king’s decision to send letters and a present.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the fact that the envoys came after hearing of Hezekiah’s recovery?

answers: Merodach-baladan
Isaiah the prophet
Hezekiah’s sons
easy.explanation: Isaiah the prophet came to King Hezekiah.
easy.q: Who came to Hezekiah after the Babylonian envoys’ visit?

answers: Egypt
Judah
Babylon
easy.explanation: Hezekiah said, “They are come from a far country unto me, even from Babylon.”
easy.q: From where did Hezekiah say the men had come?

answers: What they had seen in Hezekiah’s house
What they had eaten
Who had sent them to Jerusalem
easy.explanation: Isaiah asked, “What have they seen in thine house?”
easy.q: What did Isaiah ask about what the men had seen?

answers: Who the men were and where they had come from
What their names were and what they had eaten
How long they stayed and what they took
medium.explanation: Isaiah asked what the men had said and from where they had come.
medium.q: What two things did Isaiah ask Hezekiah to explain?

answers: They had seen only his house
They had seen everything in his house and treasures
They had seen nothing
medium.explanation: Hezekiah answered, “All that is in mine house have they seen.”
medium.q: How did Hezekiah answer Isaiah’s question about what the men had seen?

answers: A distant land
Hezekiah’s own house
A nearby place
medium.explanation: Hezekiah described Babylon as a distant or far country.
medium.q: What does the phrase “a far country” mean in this passage?

answers: After asking where the men came from, Isaiah asked what they had seen
After asking where they came from, Isaiah asked when they would return
After asking where they came from, Isaiah requested a present
challenge.explanation: Isaiah first asked about the men’s origin and then asked what they had seen in Hezekiah’s house.
challenge.q: How are Isaiah’s two questions connected?

answers: He said he had shown them everything in his treasures
He said he had not met them
He said he had shown them only the gate
challenge.explanation: His answer confirms that he had shown the envoys all his treasures.
challenge.q: Which detail in Hezekiah’s answer agrees with the previous verses?

answers: The disclosure was only partial
The disclosure was complete
The treasures had already been taken
challenge.explanation: Both the description of the visit and Hezekiah’s answer stress that he showed them everything.
challenge.q: What does the repeated statement that Hezekiah showed them everything emphasize?

paragraphs.title: The Prophecy of the Treasures Being Taken to Babylon

answers: The word of the LORD
A letter from the king of Babylon
A list of treasures
easy.explanation: Isaiah told Hezekiah to hear “the word of the Lord of hosts.”
easy.q: What did Isaiah declare to Hezekiah?

answers: Egypt
Babylon
Another distant land
easy.explanation: The prophecy says that all these things would be carried to Babylon.
easy.q: Where would Hezekiah’s possessions and his fathers’ treasures be taken?

answers: Nothing would be left
All the gold would remain
Only the household vessels would remain
easy.explanation: The prophecy says, “nothing shall be left.”
easy.q: What would remain of the treasures?

answers: He showed the treasures, and they were foretold to be taken to Babylon
He hid the treasures, and they were foretold to remain with him
He gave away the treasures, and they were foretold to be returned
medium.explanation: After Hezekiah showed his treasures, Isaiah announced that they would one day be carried to Babylon.
medium.q: What connection does the passage make between Hezekiah’s action and the prophecy?

answers: A future event
The end of the present day
The arrival of the envoys
medium.explanation: The phrase introduces a prophecy about events that would happen in the future.
medium.q: What does the phrase “Behold, the days come” introduce?

answers: The Babylonian envoys
Hezekiah’s fathers
Isaiah
medium.explanation: The prophecy includes “that which thy fathers have laid up in store until this day.”
medium.q: Who had gathered some of the treasures that would be taken?

answers: The showing of the treasures foreshadows their removal
The showing of the treasures guarantees that they will remain in Judah
The showing of the treasures cancels Isaiah’s prophecy
challenge.explanation: The display of the treasures can be understood as foreshadowing Babylon’s future seizure of them.
challenge.q: What symbolic meaning can be seen in the treasures shown to Babylon later being taken to Babylon?

answers: Only part of the silver
All the possessions and everything gathered by the fathers
Only the spices and precious ointment
challenge.explanation: The prophecy includes everything in Hezekiah’s house and everything stored by his fathers.
challenge.q: What is the extent of the loss described in the prophecy?

answers: Only as the place from which the envoys came
As the power that would receive and control the treasures
As a place with no connection to Judah
challenge.explanation: Babylon is presented as the destination to which Judah’s treasures would be carried and as the coming ruling power.
challenge.q: How is Babylon presented in this prophecy?

paragraphs.title: The Exile of the Descendants and Hezekiah’s Response

answers: The Babylonian envoys
Hezekiah’s descendants
Only his fathers’ treasures
easy.explanation: Isaiah said that Hezekiah’s sons who would come from him would be taken away.
easy.q: Who would be taken away to Babylon according to the prophecy?

answers: In Hezekiah’s house
In the palace of the king of Babylon
In Isaiah’s house
easy.explanation: The verse says they would be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.
easy.q: Where would Hezekiah’s descendants serve after being taken away?

answers: Good is the word of the LORD
He hid the words
He denied the prophecy
easy.explanation: Hezekiah said, “Good is the word of the Lord which thou hast spoken.”
easy.q: How did Hezekiah respond to Isaiah’s words?

answers: Because there would be peace and truth in his days
Because the treasures would remain with him
Because his sons would not be taken away
medium.explanation: Hezekiah explained, “For there shall be peace and truth in my days.”
medium.q: Why did Hezekiah regard the word of the LORD as good?

answers: Servants in the king’s palace
Messengers bringing gifts
Princes ruling Judah
medium.explanation: The descendants would serve in the palace of the king of Babylon.
medium.q: In this context, what does “eunuchs” describe?

answers: The future would include exile, while his days would have peace and truth
The future would have treasures, while his days would have exile
The future would have peace, while his days would include the exile of his descendants
medium.explanation: The prophecy describes future exile, while Hezekiah says that his own days would have peace and truth.
medium.q: What contrast appears between the prophesied future and Hezekiah’s own days?

answers: He accepted it because his own days would have peace and truth
He refused to listen to it
He thought it concerned only the treasures
challenge.explanation: Hezekiah accepted the word as good and explained that peace and truth would remain in his days.
challenge.q: What does Hezekiah’s response reveal about his attitude toward the prophecy?

answers: They would be taken away and serve in the king of Babylon’s palace
They would remain forever in Hezekiah’s house
They would be sent as envoys to Judah
challenge.explanation: The prophecy describes both their removal and their service in the Babylonian king’s palace.
challenge.q: What detail about the descendants’ future might be overlooked?

answers: It distinguishes the difficult future from the peace of Hezekiah’s remaining days
It cancels the prophecy about the descendants
It announces that the treasures will immediately be returned
challenge.explanation: Hezekiah accepts the future prophecy while noting that his own days will still have peace and truth.
challenge.q: How does the final verse relate to the prophecy about the future?
